text:
Alex Chen: seeing weird IOPS spikes on eu-west2-gpu nodes, not correlated with batch windows
Priya Patel: saw that too, GPUs failing provisioning with attach timeouts during the spike :confused:
Mike O'Neill: logs look like small random reads hitting nvme metadata paths, not our usual scrub pattern
Jen Park: could be deferred TRIM or overlayfs readdir churn after container teardown
Alex Chen: scrub-bot shows a bunch of scrubs kicked on the same shard at 00:02 UTC and 00:17 UTC repeatedly, but workload was quiet
scrub-bot: scrub-runner started job id=4857 shard=eu-west2-gnode-12 concurrency=6 trim=false
Priya Patel: interesting. can someone grep iostat around the window? iostat -x 1 5 on node showed r/s spikes of 1200 with avg r_await 0.4ms
Mike O'Neill: pasting short dmesg snippet, these NVMe SMART logs pop during the spike:
```
[6177772222.123456] nvme0: I/O 0x7fffa3 status 0x1c
[6177772222.123789] nvme0: read 4K qid 7 latency 400us
[6177772222.124000] nvme0: multipath read fallback
```
Jen Park: multipath read fallback suggests firmware retrying small ops, could amplify if janitor/overlayfs churns small files
Alex Chen: hypothesis: janitor + container gc triggers lots of metadata ops; overlayfs readdir causes underlying small reads that NVMe firmware schedules oddly => spectral 'ghost' IOPS
Priya Patel: does this explain GPU attach failure? yes — local pool IOPS starvation delays device setup and kubelet times out
Mike O'Neill: quick mitigation we used: 1) throttle scrub concurrency to 2 on eu-west2 2) temporarily route gpu-provisioning to reserve pool in us-west2 3) bump ioprio for scrubber systemd slice
Alex Chen: commands we ran (on eu-west2-gnode-12):
```
# lower concurrency
kubectl -n infra exec scrub-runner-4857 -- ./scrubctl set-concurrency 2
# set ioprio for scrub worker
systemd-run --scope -p IOSchedulingClass=best-effort -p IOPriority=5 /usr/local/bin/scrub-worker
# move new gpu requests to reserve pool
./provisioner route --from eu-west2 --to reserve-pool --reason "ghost-iops"
```
Jen Park: immediate effect: IOPS dropped 80% in 3 minutes and attach timeouts stopped, nice :tada:
Priya Patel: root cause plan: add jitter and stagger for janitor/scrub runs per-shard, and switch overlayfs teardown to batch unlink instead of readdir-heavy pattern
Mike O'Neill: also testing kernel param vm.dirty_bytes and tweak for overlayfs fsync window; early test shows fewer small reads
Alex Chen: opened infra PR for scrub scheduling and ioprio defaults: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 (WIP)
Jen Park: ops checklist for postmortem:
- document timeline and nodes impacted
- add monitoring alert for small-op IOPS spike (r/s > 800 && avg_await < 1ms)
- plan canary for scrub scheduling change
- decide on permanent ioprio profile or cgroup-throttle
Priya Patel: cost note: we briefly failed over ~120 GPU requests to reserved capacity for ~25m; estimated extra cost ~$1.1k. flag to finance?
Alex Chen: tagging finance-signal and we should add to incident cost estimate in postmortem
Mike O'Neill: ownership: Priya will own deploy of scrub schedule changes, Alex will own provisoner fallback rules, Jen will own kernel param experiments
Priya Patel: will open the canary rollout ticket and schedule for 2 small waves next Tue/Wed
Jen Park: also adding healthcheck: if local-nvme iops spike AND pending GPU attach > 5 then route to reserve automatically
Alex Chen: ok team. thanks for quick reaction. leaving this thread open for updates and postmortem notes
oncall-bot: Incident stool: INC-2026-412 created, linked to this thread
Mike O'Neill: quick note — we should audit overlayfs use in image build pipelines, there are several that do heavy small-file ops during startup
Priya Patel: yes, will include that in the audit scope
Alex Chen: closing loop: will paste postmortem link here when ready
